name: NAURU
lead: Nauru is the world's smallest republic (a country with no king), a coral dot in the Pacific. Its soil turned out to be phosphate, a plant food made from ancient seabird droppings. That made Nauru very rich. Today people rebuild among the jagged rock the mines left.

sections.geography: A coral dot in the Pacific

geo: Nauru is a flat oval of coral reef. Almost everyone lives on the narrow coast. Inland, a plateau (high flat land) rises about 30 metres. Mining left it bare.
Nauru has no rivers. Buada Lagoon, a quiet pond lined with palms, holds almost all its fresh water. The ocean drops deep just offshore.
animals: The Nauru reed warbler is a small brown bird. It lives nowhere else on Earth. Mining destroyed most of its forest, so it is now at risk.
Great frigatebirds snatch fish in mid-flight above the coast. Under the waves, reef fish, sea turtles and trevally fish dart around the coral.
culture: Nauruans belong to 12 ancient clans (big families). You join your mum's clan, because families follow the mother's side. Feasts bring everyone together over fresh fish and coconut.
Chants and dances keep old stories alive. Families weave leaf mats and baskets. Weightlifting is a proud national sport. Nauruan lifters have won Commonwealth Games medals.
history: Settlers from nearby islands arrived around 1000 BCE. British captain John Fearn named it Pleasant Island in 1798. Germany claimed it in 1888. Britain, Australia and Japan ruled it later.
Mining began in 1907, and by the 1970s Nauru was the richest country per person. The phosphate ran out by the early 2000s. Nauru became independent in 1968.
wows: Only two countries are smaller than Nauru: Vatican City and Monaco.
You can drive around the island in about 20 minutes.
Nauru's wealth began with millions of years of seabird poo.
Nauru was so rich in the 1970s that it ran its own airline.
Nauru has no official capital, but government offices are in Yaren.
Only about 200 tourists visit Nauru a year, among the fewest on Earth.
The flag's 12-point star stands for Nauru's 12 clans.

myths.fact: It makes good plant food. Nauru's phosphate went to farms in Australia and New Zealand.

myths.myth: Tiny countries get no say at the United Nations
myths.fact: Nauru joined in 1999. Its vote counts the same as China's.
